subject: physics_2
question_text: Why is manganin used for making standard resistors?

verification.note: The mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: manganin (a Cu-Mn-Ni alloy) has a very small temperature coefficient of resistance and a fairly high resistivity, so its resistance stays nearly constant as it warms in use — the property a standard resistor needs. The book cites only the small α; the high resistivity line is kept as an unmarked extra.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the property: very small temperature coefficient of resistance.
steps.why: Every resistor warms up when current flows through it. A material whose resistance barely responds to that warming is the only kind that can hold a fixed value.
common_mistakes: Saying manganin has zero resistance. It has a definite resistance; what is small is the CHANGE with temperature.
Writing low resistivity. Manganin's resistivity is fairly high; its temperature coefficient is what is small.

recall.must_convey: That manganin's temperature coefficient of resistance is very small, so its resistance hardly changes with temperature.
accept: resistance almost does not change with temperature
alpha is very less for manganin
reject: the value marked on it stays true

steps.memory_tip: Manganin: small α. That one property is the whole answer.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Connect the property to the job: the marked value must stay true while the resistor warms.
steps.why: The mark is for the connection, not the fact — a standard is only a standard if its value does not drift while it is being used.
common_mistakes: Stopping at alpha is small without saying why a standard resistor needs that.

recall.must_convey: That a standard resistor must keep its marked value while it warms in use, and manganin's constant resistance gives exactly that.
accept: the marked value stays true while it heats
so it is used to prepare standard resistors

steps.memory_tip: Property then purpose: small α, so the marked value never drifts.

insider_note: One property (very small α) plus one connection (the marked value stays true while it warms) — two marks, two sentences.
